phase: DEV-247 River Development Agent Controlled Executor Capability Foundation
commitMessage: DEV-247: Build River Development Agent controlled executor capability foundation
architectureStatus: Generation III controlled executor capability foundation
predecessor: DEV-246 River Development Agent controlled execution intelligence governance executor admission foundation
objective: Create a deterministic controlled executor capability foundation that consumes a trusted executor-admitted DEV-246 governance record and derives an explicit fail-closed capability envelope describing which classes of downstream executor behavior could be eligible for later authorization, while preserving execution-request provenance, human authorization evidence, repository authorization evidence, explicit approval evidence, approved execution scope, and strict separation between capability eligibility and actual execution.
architecturalDecision: DEV-246 establishes executor admission eligibility without performing execution.
DEV-247 introduces an explicit capability envelope between executor admission and any future executor implementation.
Capability eligibility describes possible downstream controlled behavior but does not itself authorize or perform that behavior.
No capability may exceed the approved execution scope inherited from predecessor governance evidence.
Capabilities are denied by default unless explicitly represented by the governed capability contract.
Repository mutation, command execution, commit, push, deployment, and autonomous execution remain downstream concerns requiring separate authorization and implementation.
Capability derivation cannot create new human authorization, repository authorization, approval, or scope.
invariants: Capability derivation requires trusted DEV-246 executor-admission evidence.
Capability derivation requires executor admission.
Capability derivation requires preserved authorization.
Capability derivation requires preserved handoff and dispatch readiness.
Capability derivation requires an unblocked predecessor record.
Capability derivation requires governed execution-request evidence.
Capability policy is deny-by-default.
Capability eligibility does not imply capability authorization.
Capability eligibility does not imply capability execution.
Capability derivation preserves human authorization evidence.
Capability derivation preserves repository authorization evidence.
Capability derivation preserves explicit approval evidence.
Capability derivation preserves approved execution scope.
Capability derivation cannot expand approved execution scope.
Capability derivation cannot create command execution authority.
Capability derivation cannot create repository modification authority.
Capability derivation cannot create commit authority.
Capability derivation cannot create push authority.
Capability derivation cannot create deployment authority.
Capability derivation cannot create autonomous execution authority.
